summary: Reworked the mix-rate bounds task so a previously valid stored file stays loadable: the stored-settings layer migrates a stored overlap_preservation_rate of 100 to 99, while Settings::validate keeps the 1..=99 band and the UI clamps are unchanged. The migration, its tests, and the engine contract bullet are updated.

TIMING-MIX-RATE-BOUNDS-CLAMP.evidence: The 1..=99 band still holds on both live paths (parse_rate_text clamps typed input and shares with the press box; Settings::validate rejects anything outside 1..=99) and the stored layer now migrates instead of rejecting: StoredTimingSettings::overlap_preservation_rate() maps a stored 100 to 99, and TimingSettings::deserialize resolves mode from the raw stored value first so the pre-mode 100 still means Release Delay. Re-executed evidence: pre_mode_files_migrate_to_the_behavior_that_shipped asserts every legacy case passes validate() and that the full-overlap file maps to ReleaseDelay with rate 99; a_stored_whole_overlap_rate_migrates_into_the_band asserts RandomMix 100 -> 99 with validate() Ok, the legacy 100 file -> ReleaseDelay with validate() Ok, and 101 still rejected; typed_preservation_rates_clamp_to_whole_percent and an_out_of_range_mix_ratio_clamps_without_leaving_the_mode still pin input clamping to 1 and 99. docs/architecture/engine.md now records the migration instead of whole-file rejection.

risks: The migration covers exactly the old ceiling, 100: stored 0 or 101+ values still fail validate() and reject the whole file, which matches the required action and the storage policy for values that were never in band.
TimingSettings::deserialize is also the IPC path, so a runtime receiving a draft from an older UI build that still sends 100 clamps it to 99 instead of rejecting the draft.
Native on-screen validation was not performed: the acceptance evidence is unit and integration tests plus the contract document, not a desktop session.
